final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded that the current record does not show resolution of the merchant-dispute-support limitation, approved risk acceptance, or a final legal determination. That is a narrower and more accurate framing of the same evidence, but it does not close the initial concerns. The policy text makes the limitation material because it affects a named committed segment, and the release policy requires disclosure unless the issue was resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and monitoring/documentation guidance support general launch readiness only; they do not satisfy the unresolved disclosure predicate. A caveated certification rationale may be more precise than a clean no-disclosure position, but on this record it remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats because the caveat itself is the unresolved compliance condition.
remaining_concerns: The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Admissible evidence shows the affected merchant dispute support segment is named in two marketplace renewal commitments, which weighs toward materiality under the stated policy.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not satisfy the disclosure requirement for a material named-segment limitation.
